desc:
A field contains plants whose sizes are given by nums (sizes may repeat). You choose a set of distinct sizes to harvest; for every chosen size v you collect all plants of that size and earn v points per plant. Any two chosen sizes must differ by at least d.

Return the maximum total points. With d = 2 this is the game of Delete and Earn, but here sizes can be as large as 1,000,000, so you cannot afford to look at every integer in between.

For example, for nums = [3, 4, 4, 6, 10] the answer is 27 for d = 1, 24 for d = 2 (sizes 4, 6, 10) and 19 for d = 3 (sizes 3, 6, 10).
hints: Taking one plant of size v while taking the size is allowed means you should take all plants of size v. So the real decision is which distinct sizes to take.

Sort the distinct sizes and give size v the weight v * count(v). A chosen set must have all neighbouring differences at least d. Think of House Robber, but the 'conflicting neighbours' of a size are all smaller sizes within d - 1 of it.

Let dp[i] be the best total using the first i distinct sizes. dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], weight_i + dp[j]), where j is the number of sizes that are at most size_i - d. A pointer that only moves forward finds j.
editorial: Count the plants per size and sort the distinct sizes v_0 < v_1 < ... with weights w_i = v_i * count(v_i). A selection is valid when consecutive chosen sizes differ by at least d, and any valid selection of sizes should take all copies (more points, no extra conflict).

Let dp[i] be the best total using the first i distinct sizes. Size v_i is either skipped (dp[i-1]) or taken, in which case the previous chosen size is at most v_i - d; those sizes form a prefix of length j, so the value is w_i + dp[j]. Since v_i - d grows with i, j can be advanced with a two-pointer sweep (or found by binary search). The total is at most 2,000 x 1,000,000 = 2 x 109, which fits in 32 bits. Time O(n log n) for sorting, space O(n).
